correctness.rationale: A bipartite neighborhood complex decomposes by parity, and the good-cover nerve on either shore is the other shore, giving homotopy equivalence. Unique center for any triple of neighbors permits a global facetwise collapse to a 2-complex. The full unpunctured cube is simply connected by converting halved-cube edges to cube-generator edges through triangle relations and filling coordinate squares; removing a center facet deletes only triangular relations whose boundaries are explicitly filled. For a second deletion, attaching graphs are K_n, K_n minus one edge at d=2, or K_(n-1) at d=1, and their triangle cycles bound in the survivor, except a d=3 missing-vertex triangle filled by a specified seven-triangle disk using a fourth coordinate. Each nullhomotopic facet attachment contributes beta1 of its graph to the sphere count. Hurewicz, 2-dimensional collapse and homology Whitehead yield integral wedges. Independently enumerated face Euler characteristics n=3,4 and both parity shores with exact Hamming-distance case distinction; n>=5 infinite proof is topological, not numeric extrapolation.

final_claim: For two deleted distinct vertices of the Boolean cube Q_n, n>=4, the ordinary open-neighborhood complex has two homotopy equivalent parity components each a wedge of b_n(d)=mu_n-C(n-1,2)-e_n(d) copies of S2, with e_n(d) piecewise C(n-2,2) (d=1), C(n-1,2)-1 (d=2), C(n-1,2) (d>=3); the exceptional n=3 antipodal deletion gives two S1 components.
